form.label: Consumption Estimates
form.description: Estimates license consumption per day, per month, and per year from a recent observation window, for cases where _internal doesn't hold a true 365-day history yet (or to project forward for renewal sizing). Three methods are shown side by side for each period - a simple average, a trend-adjusted forecast, and a conservative (buffer) estimate - because a single day's usage is too noisy (batch jobs, weekday/weekend swings) to extrapolate from directly.

input.label: Baseline window (history used for the estimate)

search.query: `license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | bin _time span=1d | stats dc(_time) as Days
`license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | bin _time span=1d | stats sum(GB) as GB by _time | stats avg(GB) as AvgGB | eval EstimateGB=round(AvgGB,2)

`license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | timechart span=1d sum(GB) as GB | predict GB as predicted algorithm=LLT future_timespan=30 | where isnull(GB) AND isnotnull(predicted) | stats avg(predicted) as TrendAvgGB | eval EstimateGB=round(TrendAvgGB,2)
`license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | bin _time span=1d | stats sum(GB) as GB by _time | stats perc95(GB) as P95GB | eval EstimateGB=round(P95GB,2)
`license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | bin _time span=1d | stats sum(GB) as GB by _time | stats avg(GB) as AvgGB | eval EstimateGB=round(AvgGB*30,0)

`license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | timechart span=1d sum(GB) as GB | predict GB as predicted algorithm=LLT future_timespan=30 | where isnull(GB) AND isnotnull(predicted) | stats avg(predicted) as TrendAvgGB | eval EstimateGB=round(TrendAvgGB*30,0)
`license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | bin _time span=1d | stats sum(GB) as GB by _time | stats perc95(GB) as P95GB | eval EstimateGB=round(P95GB*30,0)
`license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | bin _time span=1d | stats sum(GB) as GB by _time | stats avg(GB) as AvgGB | eval EstimateGB=round(AvgGB*365,0)

`license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | timechart span=1d sum(GB) as GB | predict GB as predicted algorithm=LLT future_timespan=30 | where isnull(GB) AND isnotnull(predicted) | stats avg(predicted) as TrendAvgGB | eval EstimateGB=round(TrendAvgGB*365,0)
`license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | bin _time span=1d | stats sum(GB) as GB by _time | stats perc95(GB) as P95GB | eval EstimateGB=round(P95GB*365,0)

panel.title: Daily Consumption - History & 30-Day Forecast (95% confidence band)

search.query: `license_usage_base` | `license_usage_gb` | timechart span=1d sum(GB) as GB | predict GB as predicted algorithm=LLT future_timespan=30 upper95=upper95 lower95=lower95

panel.title: How to read these numbers
panel.html:
• Daily / Monthly / Annual: the same three methods below are computed once per period - daily is the raw per-day figure, monthly multiplies it by 30, annual by 365 - so all three periods stay consistent with each other.
  • Simple Estimate: average daily consumption over the baseline window. Easy to explain, but flat - it assumes tomorrow looks like the average of the past, ignoring any growth or decline trend.
  • Trend-Adjusted Estimate: uses Splunk's built-in predict command (local-level-trend algorithm) to forecast the next 30 days from the baseline window, then averages that forecasted rate. This is the number to use for renewal sizing, since it reacts to onboarding of new data sources.
  • Conservative Estimate: the 95th-percentile day - a buffer figure for clients who want to size against their heaviest days rather than the average, to avoid recurring near-quota warnings.
  • All three depend on the selected baseline window actually holding data. If Days of History Used is much smaller than the window (e.g. 20 days shown for a 90-day window), _internal retention is cutting the history short - treat the estimate as low-confidence and consider enabling the summary-index rollup in savedsearches.conf to build up longer history over time.
